correctness.rationale: The stated toral map is two continuous piecewise-affine orthogonal slope-±2 tent shears. Its exact fourth iterate can be subdivided into 2,337 full-dimensional rational polygons with integer-affine return maps. I inspected the actual checker.py and the proof of area-one coverage, convex half-plane clipping, singular-return analysis, torus-edge identifications, and exact period-2 exclusion. The source certificate explicitly reduces 574 nonsingular incidence solutions to 336 toral fixed representatives, removes 16 points of period dividing 2, giving 320 primitive points or 80 cycles. The nine singular affine cells yield only the four known period-two segments or no fixed locus; no uncounted positive-dimensional primitive-four family. The differentiated 256 primitive points have trace counts −574:128, +578:64, +178:64 and 64 switching points. All three smooth traces have absolute value >2 and determinant 1, hence the 64 differentiable cycles are hyperbolic. This is a complete finite rational subdivision argument, not evidence from an unbounded numerical orbit sample. The entire exact source checker was read but not independently executed in this run.
